references.text: God promises Abram to make him a great nation, which forms the basis of the promise to become 'a father of many nations' in Gen 17:5.
God promises Abram descendants as numerous as the stars, emphasizing the promise to become 'a father of many nations'.
God declares His covenant with Abram and promises that he will be a father of many peoples—the very basis for the name change in verse 5.
Paul quotes directly from Gen 17:5 and calls Abraham 'a father of many nations', linking this to faith in God who gives life to the dead.
Paul describes how Abraham, against hope, believed with hope that he would become 'a father of many nations', in accordance with the promise.
Paul shows that all who belong to Christ are Abraham's offspring and heirs according to the promise, extending the fulfillment of the promise of many nations.
The Levites remind us that God chose Abram and changed his name to Abraham, a direct reference to the name change in Gen 17:5.
Isaiah confirms and summarizes the theological core of the name change: God's calling of one man to become a father of many.
The direct parallel in the same chapter shows that the name change to Abraham was part of a shared covenant promise to the couple.
It illustrates a recurring biblical pattern where God's changing of a name marks a fundamental shift in identity and role.
It confirms and expands on the universal dimension of the promise embedded in Abraham's name change.
